subject: MAP alignment: security gate sequencing + DPA retention clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@cobaltfinance.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hale <t.hale@cobaltfinance.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & compliance gates — timeline constraints

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Cobalt's procurement and security teams asked me to pull the MAP into a single doc so we can track the remaining security gates and close timelines. Two timing constraints to flag up front: procurement wants a signed DPA and MPA commitments by 2028-04-28, and our CTO wants a SOC 2 walkthrough completed before the production integration window (target week of 2028-05-08).

A few specific asks we need to capture in the MAP:
- Clear SOC 2 evidence items and who at Redwood will present each artifact (report, control owner contact, test evidence).
- SIG/CAIQ mapping for the API flows we plan to use (streaming + embeddings).
- DPA redlines: retention windows, deletion workflows, right-to-audit and KMS responsibilities.
- Data residency / escrow question: do you support EU-only residency for tokenized request/response logs? If not, what's the retention carveout?

Can you share a MAP that shows the gating order (which items we block on vs parallel work), and any proposed fallback (hosted -> dedicated -> private) that keeps our integration timeframe intact? If you can get us a draft by EOD Monday (2028-04-17) that'd help legal and procurement start the redline pass.

Appreciate it — copying Tom from Legal to keep the DPA thread moving.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rios
Head of Platform Integrations
Cobalt Finance

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@cobaltfinance.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & compliance gates — timeline constraints

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the timeline. Draft MAP attached (Cobalt-MAP-v1.2.xlsx) and uploaded to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/rdw/Cobalt/MAP-v1.2.

High-level summary of the MAP I attached:
- Critical path (blocking): DPA-sign (legal), SOC 2 walkthrough + control owner confirmations, SIG/CAIQ artifact mapping.
- Parallel work: perf validation in staging, integration smoke tests, RBAC config.
- Fallbacks: if hosted capacity becomes constrained we'll propose temporary routing to a compatible quantized model on Dedicated for the first 48 hours of cutover; Private deployment is an option but will push final cutover by ~3–4 weeks.

Security/compliance gate specifics (excerpts):
1) SOC 2: we list the report (most recent Type II), named control owners (security@redwood.ai for infra controls; runtime@redwood.ai for serving/runtime), and a proposed 60-minute walkthrough slot. Evidence items include: SOC 2 report PDF, change control log extract (last 12 months), incident response runbook, and deployment/configuration snapshots.

2) SIG/CAIQ: attached spreadsheet maps each CAIQ control to Redwood artifacts for the API flows you flagged (streaming generation, embeddings ingest). We'll highlight open controls where we need either a customer attestation or a product change.

3) DPA & retention: proposed default retention windows in MAP: request logs (30 days), generated content cache (90 days), archival snapshot for debugging (365 days, metadata-only after 90 days). We added a carveout section for EU residency: if EU-only residency is required we can scope a Private deployment (additional infra + lead time) or negotiate a 90-day max retention with strict geo-fencing.

4) KMS & key management: we support CMK via customer KMS in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed CMKs but provide attestations and key rotation policy.

Next steps I propose:
- Legal redline on the DPA (we'll track via Docs / DocuSign).
- Confirm one SOC 2 walkthrough slot (we have availability Wed 2028-04-19 10am or Thu 2028-04-20 3pm PT).
- Kimberly will sync on SIG/CAIQ open items and note which need engineering commitments.

I've CC'd Markus (security lead) for the SOC 2 walkthrough details and Kimberly for contract/review support. Please let me know which DPA approach you prefer (redline vs annotated comments).

Thanks — attaching: Cobalt-MAP-v1.2.xlsx (map), short artifact inventory in sheet two.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Attachments: Cobalt-MAP-v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Elena Rios <elena.rios@cobaltfinance.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & compliance gates — timeline constraints

Thanks Sofia / Elena — quick technical clarifications so we can lock the SOC 2 walkthrough scope: 

- Walkthrough scope: will cover production control plane and serving runtime. Elena, please confirm whether you need staging evidence for the same controls or only production artifacts. If procurement needs both, that increases prep time by ~3 business days to sanitize snapshots.

- Evidence granularity: procurement typically accepts the SOC 2 report + sample test evidence (change control logs, ticket IDs, deployment hashes). If Cobalt wants continuous export of request/response logs to your SIEM, we can enable an export stream for a 30-day window (PII redaction configurable). Let me know which you prefer — export vs spot-delivery of artifacts.

- Retention options — we recommend default: request logs 30d (hot), cached model outputs 90d, archived snapshots (metadata-only) 365d. If Cobalt requires EU-only residency for logs, we need to scope a Dedicated pool in eu-west with the associated infra cost and a ~3 week lead time.

- KMS: for Hosted, we can provide a KMS attestation and rotate envelope keys. For custodial-hosted keys we would need an HSM attestation; if you require Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) that's supported in Dedicated/Private only.

I'll prepare a short checklist for the SOC 2 walkthrough (control owners, evidence location, sample IDs) and circulate it by EOD.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Tom Hale <t.hale@cobaltfinance.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rios <elena.rios@cobaltfinance.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & compliance gates — timeline constraints (DPA redline attached)

Team — attaching an annotated DPA with our initial redlines (DPA-redline-annotated.docx). High level comments: 

1) Retention & deletion workflow: we need a clear deletion SLA in the DPA (redwood to expose deletion API + confirmation event). Prefer deletion within 5 business days for request logs; longer windows for archived snapshots are OK if metadata-only after 90 days.

2) Right to audit: we will accept a SOC 2 Type II report for the initial phase, but we need audit-right language for a future on-site or remote audit within a 12–18 month window if risk profile increases.

3) KMS and key custody: we prefer BYOK for keys that protect customer-provided encryption material; if BYOK is not available in Hosted we need a carveout showing Dedicated/Private as the path.

4) Data residency: the redline proposes a maximum 90-day retention for any logs leaving the EU if EU-only residency can't be guaranteed. If Redwood can guarantee EU residency for logs in Hosted via eu-west routing and geofence, we can discuss extending that window.

Please confirm whether Redwood can deliver the deletion confirmation event (webhook / signed ack) and whether you can accept a two-week timeline to review and respond to these redlines (we're trying to keep the procurement target of 2028-04-28).

Tom Hale
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Cobalt Finance
